context: Practice interview for a backend developer role at Orbit Pay (invented company). My notes: 5 years of experience with Python and Node, no Go. Led a payment service migration that cut cloud cost by 40 percent, leading a team of 4. Production incident story: a payment outage, found the cause in 20 minutes, wrote a postmortem. Reason for leaving: limited growth path to a lead role. Weakness: delegating, now using written handoffs. Do not state a salary number. Questions I want to ask: on-call, team growth plan, how success is measured.

lines.text: Hi Gil, thank you for the time. I am happy to be here.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Welcome Dan. I have your CV. I see eight years of experience, is that right?
It is five years, mostly with Python and Node.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Got it. Why are you leaving your current job?
I want more growth. At my current company there is no clear path to a lead role.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Makes sense. Tell me about a time you handled a production incident.
We had a payment outage. I found the cause in twenty minutes and then wrote a postmortem.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Good. I would like to hear about your leadership experience as well.
I led the payment service migration with a team of four people.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: And the results?
It cut our cloud cost by forty percent.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Impressive. Our stack is mostly Go, and you have no Go experience. That worries me.
I understand. I learned Node in a few months, and I can learn Go the same way.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Let me ask a design question. How would you design a rate limiter for an API?
I would clarify requirements first, then use a token bucket per client in a shared cache.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: And how do you make a payment request idempotent?
With an idempotency key stored with the result, so a retry returns the same response.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Good. What are your salary expectations?
I would like to hear the range for the role first.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Fair. Yael, can you bring us some water?

lines.speaker: Yael
lines.text: Sure, one minute.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Thanks. By the way, the weather is terrible today.
It really is.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: What is your biggest weakness?
I used to hold on to tasks, so now I use written handoffs when I delegate.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Fine. We recently raised funding and we plan to double the team.
Congratulations. How does that change the team plan?

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: We will hire in stages. Can you send me your portfolio link?
Yes, I will send my portfolio.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: I will give you an answer within a week.
Thank you. Can I ask about on-call?

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: We can come back to that. Do you have other questions for us?
Yes. What does on-call look like, and how do you measure success in the first six months?

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: On-call is one week in six, and success is measured by delivery and quality.
That helps. I will also send my portfolio today.

lines.speaker: Gil
lines.text: Thank you Dan.
Thank you, Gil.
